_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: Humanity sent a message to the stars as part of a ceremony.
beats.note: Arecibo broadcast it to mark the remodelling of its telescope. It was a demonstration of technology, not a serious attempt at conversation.

beats.text: Frank Drake wrote it, with help.
beats.note: Carl Sagan and other colleagues contributed to the design.

beats.context: The length of the message. It is 73 times 23, both prime, which hints at how to fold it into a picture.

beats.text: Numbers, DNA, a stick figure and the telescope.
beats.note: It counts one to ten, gives the atomic numbers of five elements, shows DNA, a human 1.764 metres tall, a population of about four billion, the Solar System and the dish.

beats.text: The whole thing took under three minutes.
beats.note: It went out at 10 bits a second.

beats.text: One number was already out of date.
beats.note: The message gave a figure for human DNA base pairs that was believed correct in 1974. The count is now known to be about 3.2 billion.

beats.text: It will take more than 20,000 years to arrive.
beats.note: The target is M13, a star cluster. The SETI Institute says it is unlikely to prompt a reply.

beats.text: The most powerful broadcast we aimed at the stars was part of a ceremony.
